prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1415; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a low-speed head-on collision. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Police report obtained. It confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision and records the scene as described on first notice.

Entry 3: Driver confirmed as a named driver on the policy. Coverage was in force on the date of loss, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 4: Photos from the scene reviewed. They confirm several key details of the impact, though no independent witnesses have come forward to add to the account.

Entry 5: Vehicle damage reviewed against the reported impact. The damage pattern matches the described collision, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or inspection records.

Entry 6: Medical records received for a knee injury. The injury is consistent in kind and force with the mechanism of this crash.

Entry 7: Records also show a minor strain in the same area several years ago, which healed fully with no ongoing treatment at that time.

Entry 8: Treatment has run somewhat longer than is typical for this type of knee injury. The treating provider's notes explain the course of care, and a medical review has been requested.

Entry 9: Claimant's statement obtained through counsel. Minor details were added since the first report, but the core account of the collision has stayed the same across each telling.

Entry 10: File remains open pending the medical review and receipt of the remaining treatment billing. Next follow-up is set with counsel once those items are received.
